Business one, business two

BZ-01 / The clock

Every business gets read by its age, and its age starts counting the day you file it.

How old yours is on the day your personal file is ready decides what the business side adds.

  • Our engine prints this line for a file that still has credit work ahead of it.
  • Every business gets read by its AGE, and that age only starts counting on the day you file it. Until that day, the clock on your business sits at zero.
  • How old your business is on the day your personal file is ready decides what the business side adds. That day is coming, so the clock matters now.
  • Look at what our engine prints for a file that still has credit work ahead of it. It tells you to form the LLC NOW, so it ages while that work runs.
  • That line comes straight from the engine's own rules. It reads every business in age bands, and a brand new business sits in the lowest band it has.
  • That means the months you spend on your personal file can count TWICE. Your credit work runs, and your business gets older over those same months.

BZ-02 / Five checks

Of the five checks on a business, age is the only one that grows on its own.

  • Two of the five read your personal file, so those pass when your own file is ready.
  • The name and the industry code go on file once, as part of setting the business up.
  • Age keeps counting up from the filing date, and the engine's top band starts at 24 months.
  • Here's what's really going on with your business. Our engine gives every business FIVE checks of its own, and every one of them counts the same.
  • Two of them read your personal file. One asks if that file is fundable. The other looks on your own report for a card with a big limit, open since at least two years back.
  • Then come the name and the industry code, which are paperwork. Both go on file once, when the business gets set up, and then they're done.
  • That leaves AGE. It counts up from your filing date by itself. It keeps counting while you work on everything else on your plan.
  • The engine's top band starts at 24 MONTHS. A business filed late gets there late, no matter how fast you finish the rest of your file.

BZ-03 / The cost

A business 24 months or older counts four times what a brand new one counts.

  • Under 12 months, the business side counts at half. From 12 to 24 months, it counts in full. At 24 months and up, it counts double.
  • With no filing date on record, the business side counts at zero.
  • Age is how our engine sizes the business side, and every bank still rules on its own applications.
  • Here's what filing late COSTS you. Our engine sizes the business side by age, and its top band is four times its bottom one.
  • Look at the bars. Under 12 months old, the business side counts at HALF. From 12 to 24 months, it counts in full.
  • At 24 months and up, it counts DOUBLE. Same business, same owner, same personal file, and the only thing that changed is how long it's been on the books.
  • And if there's no filing date on record, the engine counts the business side at zero. So the date has to be real, and it has to be on file.
  • Every month you wait to file costs you. On the day your personal file is ready, a late filing sits in a lower band.
  • That difference is money your business goes without. It's the next hire, a bigger job, and ads that keep running every month.

BZ-04 / The order

Business one gets primed first, then business two, once your personal file is ready.

  • Each business keeps its own count and its own place on your plan, never blended into one figure.
  • Business one gets primed and ready first, then business two, and each one adds fundability.
  • File early, and each business already has age behind it when its turn comes.
  • Here's how the Blueprint handles it. Your personal file gets primed FIRST, because two of every business's checks are read straight off it.
  • Then business one gets primed and READY. It has its own five checks and its own count, kept apart from your personal file.
  • Then business two, on its own count again. The engine never blends your businesses into one score or one total.
  • Each business stands on its own count. Every one you add brings more FUNDABILITY, and the count on the ones before it stays the same.
  • You filed early, so each business already has months of age on it when its turn comes. And that age keeps counting toward the top band.
  • An AI coach follows your open step. When something needs a person, someone on the Fundhub team picks it up. Nothing on your plan sits still.

BZ-05 / The step

Two days in, this sample file had its LLC filed and its business checking open.

  • The step asks you to file with your Secretary of State, then send the confirmation to the Fundhub team.
  • The second business step is a checking account opened in the LLC's name.
  • Both steps are yours to do, and the checklist marks each one as you finish it.
  • This is the real Blueprint checklist, on a SAMPLE file at month six. Look at the two business steps, and look at when they got done.
  • The LLC step was done two days into the plan. The business checking account was opened that same day, ahead of almost everything else.
  • Filing the LLC means filing with your Secretary of State, then sending the confirmation to the Fundhub team. The checking account goes in the LLC's NAME.
  • Both steps are yours, done in your own name. The checklist marks each one as you finish it, so you always see where you stand.
  • That sample business got older the whole time its personal file was being worked on. By month six, it had close to six months of age on it.
  • When the personal file is READY, that business already has months behind it. Then you fund yourself, with your file and your business both working for you.
  • That capital goes into the business itself. It pays for the hire you've held off on and the bigger jobs, while your own savings stay put.

BZ-06 / Your call

On your strategy call, your business gets read right next to your personal file.

  • Have your company's legal name, its months in business and its monthly revenue ready. Then the business side gets read on the call too.
  • If you don't have a business yet, you still work with us, because your personal file goes first either way.
  • You leave knowing which age band your business sits in, and whether filing now is your next step.
  • Remember the clock on your business? On your strategy CALL, you find out exactly where yours sits, right next to your personal file.
  • Bring three things: the legal name of your company, how long it's been open, and its average revenue each month. They take a minute to look up.
  • With those three, the business side gets read on the call too. You see how much you qualify for based on where you're at right now.
  • If you don't have a business yet, you still work with us. Your personal file goes first either way, and funding works off a personal file by itself.
  • Either way, you leave knowing which age band your business is in today. You also know if filing it NOW is the first move on your plan.
  • A computer works best for the call. Your file and your business sit side by side on one big screen while we go through them together.
